QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_11

question.text: Mr. Arvind Mehta runs Himalaya Arbitrage Fund. Risk-free rate is 7%, expected market return is 13%, fund beta is 0.8. What is the CAPM required return for the fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: CAPM: E(Ri) = Rf + beta*(Rm - Rf) = 7% + 0.8*(13% - 7%) = 7% + 0.8*6% = 7% + 4.8% = 11.8%. The Trap: (B) 13.4% adds beta*Rm instead of beta*(Rm-Rf). (C) 10.4% uses (Rm-Rf)*0.6. (D) 12.6% double-counts Rf. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D, XXI-B, XV and VIII all test the same E(Ri)=Rf+beta*(Rm-Rf) identity. The numbers change; the formula doesn't. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a market-neutral Cat III book with beta ~ 0, CAPM implies required return ~ Rf — yet LPs demand 12%+. The gap is the ALPHA expectation; your HWM crystallisation and 2-and-20 economics must be pitched as compensation for DELIVERED alpha, not for bearing beta.
